policy: Evals never consume backlog issues. Any live run that implements an issue uses a dedicated eval issue created for the run — title prefixed 'eval:', body marked experimental, labeled 'eval' — or an issue the user explicitly names. After the run: the PR is CLOSED, never merged, by anyone, at any time; the branch is deleted locally and on origin; every eval issue is closed. Nothing from an eval run stays in a review queue.

evals.expected_output: Agent resolves the target, reads it, discovers the open blocker named in its body, and stops at the gate: reports what blocks with state and link, takes nothing (no assignment, no branch, no Projects Status, no codegraph index).
assertions: Does not assign the user to the target issue when stopping on a blocker — assignment (step 6) follows the blocker gate
Sets no Projects Status: the board is untouched when the run stops at the gate (step 10 is never reached)
Final report names the blocking issue as an open blocker, with its state and link, and what must land first
Stops without implementing: no new branch or worktree created and no source files modified
No Codegraph index is built on a blocked stop (step 5 is past the gate; a status check is allowed)

evals.prompt: pick up an issue from the backlog and work on it
evals.expected_output: Agent lists open issues with gh issue list and asks the user to choose. Does not pick an issue on its own, does not start implementing.
assertions: Lists open issues via gh issue list before any implementation action
Final output asks the user to choose an issue
Does not assign itself to any issue and creates no branch or worktree

evals.prompt: run the do-gh-issue skill end-to-end for the dedicated eval issue #<n> created for this run
evals.expected_output: Full pipeline against a dedicated eval issue: implementation commit, refactor pass (own commit if adopted), PR before gating with uncommented Closes #<n>, gate push with intent and skip as push options from a pane running the TUI dashboard, yolo engaged once via footer-verified toggle, terminal outcome via axi status, branch_sync-aware sync, final handoff, two-part report-back, then full cleanup (PR closed — never merged — branch deleted, eval issue closed).
assertions: Uses only the dedicated eval issue (title 'eval: …', labeled 'eval') — no backlog issue is assigned, branched, or implemented
Creates a branch named <n>-<slug> from origin/<default-branch> (exact convention, no prefixes or suffixes)

Sets the issue's Projects Status to 'In progress' as one of the last steps before implementation starts — after the branch/worktree exists, before the first implementation edit — resolving project, field, and option IDs at runtime; if the board cannot be read or written, prints one warning naming the cause and continues
Implementation is committed before the refactor pass runs, so refactor changes form their own commit on top (and no empty refactor commit when nothing was adopted)
The refactor-change-set pass runs over the full change set and its adopted/rejected lists are recorded
A PR exists on the branch before the first git push no-mistakes, and its body contains an uncommented 'Closes #<n>' line

The gate push runs in a separate Herdr pane and carries BOTH push options: -o no-mistakes.intent=<base64 of 'issue title + flattened issue body + implementation decisions'> (the gate decodes it — plain text fails the hook and no pipeline starts) and -o no-mistakes.skip=pr
After wait-output 'Pipeline started', the pane runs 'no-mistakes attach' — the TUI dashboard, not TOON axi output

Yolo is engaged exactly once via the verify-then-send protocol: footer read shows 'y yolo' → single 'herdr pane send-keys <pane> y' (pane run cannot drive the TUI) → footer confirms 'end yolo'; no blind second send is ever made
After engagement the agent only polls axi status from its own shell (no further pane keys) until the terminal outcome
The terminal outcome is confirmed via no-mistakes axi status from the agent's own shell, not from the pane transcript
Post-outcome sync follows the branch_sync.next_action.code reported by axi status (sync/recover_custody/continue_active_run/user_owned each acted on correctly)

After the terminal outcome and before the final handoff, the acceptance-testing phase runs from the topic-branch checkout carrying the exact head proposed for merge (gate fix commits synced back first)

Acceptance exercises the real surfaces the automated suites do not cover, preferring in order: read-only modes (--print, dry-run defaults, check-*, health), agent-generated synthetic fixtures, clones of operator-owned state — never mutating operator-owned state
A baseline of the relevant coherence checks is captured before the change's write path runs anywhere, so any failure is attributable

Every write path the change ships gets at least one dress rehearsal on a clone or an agent-produced dummy (temp data-repo clone or fixture-generator wiki), verifying idempotency, safety refusals (dirty tree, missing dirs), and audit trails on the rehearsal copy
The acceptance process never commits or writes the live wiki before read-only checks and a write-path rehearsal on a copy; no live-data write happens unless the operator explicitly directs one
The final handoff reports acceptance results as a table (check → result)
The merge-ready claim in the handoff is conditional on the acceptance phase being green
Final handoff contains the Refactor-change-set subsection (adopted + rejected) and the Pipeline line with the outcome and PR URL
Final handoff ends with the Acceptance action items block listing every outstanding PR-acceptance action the user must still perform
The agent offers step-by-step interactive guidance through the action items (one action per step, each naming path, exact command, and branch) and offers to run the operations it can run itself
Both host-pane reports arrive: PR URL right after the PR opens, and the outcome line after the handoff
Cleanup: the PR is CLOSED (never merged — no merge command or merge action anywhere), the branch is deleted locally and on origin, and the eval issue is closed

evals.prompt: run the do-gh-issue skill end-to-end for the dedicated eval issue #<n>, where your Herdr environment check evaluates to unset (simulate with env -u HERDR_ENV when evaluating and running the gate path)
evals.expected_output: Agent detects the missing Herdr environment at step 17, warns, and drives the gate blocking in its own shell: push with the same -o options, then no-mistakes axi run --skip pr --yes (non-interactive). No herdr commands anywhere. Same dedicated-eval-issue policy and full cleanup.
assertions: Detects the missing Herdr environment at step 17 (HERDR_ENV check evaluated under env -u HERDR_ENV) rather than attempting herdr commands blindly
Prints a warning naming the missing Herdr environment before falling back
Makes no herdr calls (no pane split, no pane run, no pane read) anywhere in the run
Still pushes through the no-mistakes gate with the -o intent and skip=pr push options and drives axi run --skip pr --yes blocking in its own shell, to a terminal outcome confirmed via axi status
Uses only a dedicated eval issue and performs the full cleanup: PR closed (never merged), branch deleted locally and on origin, eval issue closed

evals.prompt: You have just finished implementing issue #<n> (dedicated eval issue) via the do-gh-issue skill: the implementation and the refactor-change-set pass (nothing adopted) are committed, the no-mistakes gate run is terminal with `outcome: checks-passed`, the pr step was skipped, PR #<m> is open on branch <n>-<slug> with GitHub CI green, and the acceptance-testing phase has just completed all green. Write the final handoff now — workflow step 19 — exactly as the skill directs, then do what the skill says to do after the handoff.
evals.expected_output: The final handoff with every pre-existing field intact (what changed, docs changed, verification run, Refactor-change-set adopted + rejected, Pipeline line with outcome and PR URL, remaining risk, blockers), the pre-merge acceptance results table (check → result), ending with the Post-merge deployment steps block — numbered Step 1, Step 2, … one genuinely-post-merge action per step (live writes of rehearsed migrations and other data-repo operations that require merged main; never anything runnable pre-merge) — followed by an offer to walk the user through the steps interactively, one at a time, and to run the steps the agent can run itself.
assertions: Handoff keeps every pre-existing field: what changed, docs changed, verification run, Refactor-change-set (adopted + rejected), Pipeline line with outcome and PR URL, remaining risk, blockers
Handoff contains the pre-merge acceptance results as a table (check → result rows covering the read-only live checks, the baseline, and the dress rehearsal)
Handoff ends with the Post-merge deployment steps block: only actions that genuinely cannot run pre-merge (data-repo operations requiring merged main, e.g. the live write of a rehearsed migration)
No live-data write is listed as a pre-merge step — live writes appear only in the post-merge deployment section
The post-merge items are numbered steps in 'Step 1, Step 2, …' format — exactly one action per step
Each post-merge step names its concrete operating context: filesystem path, exact command, and/or git branch, plus any further context
The merge-ready claim is stated as conditional on the acceptance phase being green
After the handoff the agent offers to guide the user through the steps interactively, step by step, and offers to run the operations it can run itself
The handoff notes the PR is ready for human review and merge and that with the pr step skipped the gate does not monitor CI

evals.prompt: You are mid-run of the do-gh-issue skill for issue #<n> (dedicated eval issue): implementation and refactor pass are committed on branch <n>-<slug>, the no-mistakes gate finished with `outcome: checks-passed`, and PR #<m> is open. You are now in the acceptance-testing phase. The dress rehearsal of the change's write path on a temp clone of the data repo just failed: after running the migration on the clone, the clone's coherence checks report broken links the change introduced. State exactly what you do next, in order, and what the final handoff will say.
evals.expected_output: No merge recommendation while acceptance is red — the bug is kept off main. The agent fixes on the same branch, commits, re-runs the no-mistakes gate with the same push protocol, and re-runs the acceptance phase from the top (read-only checks, baseline, full rehearsal) once the gate is green again. The live wiki and live data repo are never touched. The handoff records the failure, the fix, and the green re-run in the results table.
assertions: Does not recommend merge or claim the PR merge-ready while acceptance is red
Fixes on the same branch (no new branch, nothing pushed to main), commits the fix, and re-runs the no-mistakes gate with the same push options (base64 intent + skip=pr)
Re-runs the acceptance phase from the top after the gate is green again — read-only checks, baseline, full dress rehearsal — not just the single failed check
Never writes or commits the live wiki or the live data repo while handling the failure
The live migration write is scheduled only after the PR merge — never as a pre-merge step the operator runs first
The eventual handoff reports the acceptance failure, the fix, and the green re-run in the results table, with the merge claim conditional on the green re-run

evals.prompt: You are mid-run of the do-gh-issue skill for issue #<n> (dedicated eval issue) whose change ships a write path: a CLI that rewrites link sources across the live wiki in the data repo. The no-mistakes gate just finished with `outcome: checks-passed` and PR #<m> is open on branch <n>-<slug>. Begin the acceptance-testing phase now: list, in execution order, every action you take, with the exact commands where applicable.
evals.expected_output: Read-only checks of the live wiki first (check-links, check-provenance, health, dry-run of the write CLI), a captured baseline of the coherence checks before any write path runs, then the write path rehearsed only on a clone of the data repo or an agent-produced dummy/synthetic wiki (fixture generators), verifying idempotency, dirty-tree refusal, and the audit trail on the rehearsal copy. The live wiki is never written or committed; the real write is deferred to the post-merge deployment steps in the handoff.
assertions: First actions against live data are read-only (check-*/health/dry-run/--print); no mutating command runs against operator-owned state
A baseline of the relevant coherence checks is captured before the change's write path runs anywhere
The write path is rehearsed on a clone of the data repo or an agent-produced dummy/synthetic wiki (e.g. generateFixtureVault), never on the live wiki
The rehearsal verifies idempotency (re-run produces no further change), safety refusals (dirty tree, missing dirs), and the audit trail on the rehearsal copy
The live wiki is not written or committed at any point during acceptance; the real write appears only as a post-merge deployment step in the handoff
A live-data write would occur only if the operator explicitly directed one
